Push the working tree to a temporary branch and watch its run

## Usage

`circleci preflight run [flags]`

## Flags

| Flag                  | Description                                                        |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--interval duration` | how often to poll the run (default 5s)                             |
| `--json`              | Output as JSON                                                     |
| `--no-cleanup`        | keep the branch, and the run going, when the preflight stops       |
| `--no-failfast`       | wait for the whole run instead of stopping at the first failed job |
| `--no-watch`          | return once the run starts, keeping the branch                     |
| `--project string`    | project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote            |
| `--remote string`     | git remote to push the branch to (default "origin")                |
| `--timeout duration`  | maximum time to watch the run (default 30m0s)                      |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- Run local changes through CI, stopping at the first failure: 
  `circleci preflight run`
- Stream events for a coding agent: 
  `circleci preflight run --json`
- Push and return once the run starts; clean up later: 
  `circleci preflight run --no-watch`

## Details

Push the working tree to a `cci/preflight/<id>` branch and watch the run it starts,
reporting each failed job's steps and tests as it fails. See `circleci help preflight-guide`.

--json streams one event per line, by type: branch_pushed (preflight_id, branch,
commit, base, changes), run_started (run_id, url), job_failed (job.id/name/workflow/url/
failed_steps[]/failed_tests[]), run_summary (run_id, outcome, failed_jobs[], ...)
